source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. The moment a great beacon fire is lit again and the night sky pales a little: the storyteller's hopeful main theme, in the same waltz feel as the title music, starting intimate on harp and flute and blooming into warm strings and horn. Tender, grateful and luminous, like the first hint of a dawn nobody alive has seen. Tempo 84 BPM, 3/4 time, key of G major. Instrumentation: concert harp, solo wooden flute, violins and cellos, french horn, soft timpani roll, glockenspiel and celesta sparkle. Form: harp arpeggio intro; theme on flute; strings and horn swell into the second phrase; a quiet celesta bridge; theme again with full warm orchestra settling softly. Duration: 95 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
